items.headline: Singapore braces for warmer, drier weather and higher haze risk as El Niño develops
items.summary: The Meteorological Service Singapore puts the chance of an El Niño event in 2026 at more than 80 per cent, signalling warmer temperatures, below-average rainfall and an elevated risk of transboundary haze from June to October.

items.headline: HDB launches June BTO exercise with 6,900 flats as resale prices dip for first time since 2019
items.summary: The June Build-To-Order exercise offers about 6,900 flats across Ang Mo Kio, Bishan, Bukit Merah, Sembawang and Woodlands, after the first-quarter resale price index slipped 0.1 per cent - its first decline since 2019.

items.headline: India's economy grows 7.8% in Q4 and 7.7% for FY26, keeping its fastest-growing major economy tag
items.summary: Provisional government estimates released Friday showed real GDP rising 7.8 per cent in the January-March quarter and 7.7 per cent for FY26, led by services up 9.3 per cent and industry up 8.8 per cent.

items.headline: Modi meets Venezuela's Delcy Rodríguez as India expands Venezuelan oil imports
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks with Venezuelan Vice-President Delcy Rodríguez in New Delhi on Thursday to deepen energy ties; Venezuela has climbed to among India's largest crude suppliers amid the Gulf supply shock.

items.headline: Update: Southwest monsoon advances into Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Goa
items.summary: Days after its onset over Kerala, the India Meteorological Department said on 5 June that the southwest monsoon had advanced into more of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Goa, keeping its progress broadly on schedule.

items.headline: Government sets Parliament's monsoon session for July 21 to August 12
items.summary: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the monsoon session will run from 21 July to 12 August, as the Opposition presses for a special sitting to debate Operation Sindoor.

items.headline: Update: Israel keeps striking southern Lebanon despite US-brokered deal, killing at least five
items.summary: Israeli air strikes killed at least five people across southern Lebanon on Friday and triggered fresh evacuation orders, even after a US-brokered agreement; Israel says operations will continue while Hezbollah demands a full withdrawal.

items.headline: US House votes 215-208 to limit Trump's war powers on Iran
items.summary: In a bipartisan rebuke, the House passed a war powers resolution directing the President to halt further strikes on Iran, with four Republicans joining Democrats; the measure faces long odds in the Senate and a likely veto.

items.headline: South Korea's ruling party sweeps local elections but loses Seoul
items.summary: President Lee Jae-myung's Democratic Party won 12 of 16 metropolitan mayor and governor races in the 3 June local elections, while the People Power Party held Seoul, where Mayor Oh Se-hoon was re-elected.

items.headline: EU unveils tech sovereignty package to cut reliance on US and Chinese technology
items.summary: The European Commission proposed a sweeping technological sovereignty package - including a Chips Act 2.0 and a Cloud and AI Development Act - to bolster home-grown semiconductors, cloud and AI after fears of foreign control over critical services.

items.headline: EU regulators put Nvidia's AI-chip business under antitrust scrutiny
items.summary: European Union antitrust officials are reportedly canvassing Nvidia's rivals and customers over possible bundling and abuse of its dominance in AI chips, an early-stage inquiry that stops short of a formal case.

items.headline: US adds 172,000 jobs in May as unemployment holds at 4.3%
items.summary: Nonfarm payrolls rose 172,000 in May, far above the roughly 80,000 consensus, while the jobless rate held at 4.3 per cent for a third straight month and wages rose 3.4 per cent year on year; Treasury yields jumped as odds of Fed cuts faded.

items.headline: Brent crude hovers near $95 as Strait of Hormuz crisis keeps oil elevated
items.summary: Brent traded around $95 a barrel on Friday, easing after a near 3 per cent slide the previous session on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy, even as disruption at the Strait of Hormuz keeps a risk premium on energy prices.

items.headline: England set New Zealand 254 to win first Test as Black Caps reach 36-3
items.summary: England set New Zealand a target of 254 in the opening Test at Lord's, and the Black Caps closed a wicket-filled second day on 36-3, still needing 218 runs with seven wickets in hand.

items.headline: Update: Zverev reaches French Open final and will face Cobolli
items.summary: Alexander Zverev beat Jakub Mensik 7-5, 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 to reach the Roland Garros final, where he will play Italy's Flavio Cobolli, who advanced when Matteo Arnaldi withdrew ill before their semifinal.

items.headline: Hamilton leads Ferrari 1-2 in Monaco practice ahead of qualifying
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton topped second practice for the Monaco Grand Prix with a 1:13.026, 0.111 seconds ahead of Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc and with Max Verstappen third; qualifying is Saturday and the race Sunday.

fun_fact.headline: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
fun_fact.body: Venus is the slowest-spinning planet in the Solar System: it takes about 243 Earth days to turn once on its axis, yet only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun - so a single rotation lasts longer than a Venusian year. Venus also rotates backwards relative to most planets, which means that from its surface the Sun would appear to rise in the west and set in the east.

puzzle.body: A bag holds some red marbles and some blue marbles. If you draw two marbles at random, without replacement, the probability that both are red is exactly 1/2. What is the smallest possible number of marbles in the bag, and how many of them are red?
puzzle.approach: Write the probability as a ratio of combinations, then hunt for the smallest whole numbers that make it exactly one-half.
puzzle.answer: Four marbles - three red and one blue. The chance that both draws are red is (r/n) x ((r-1)/(n-1)); with 3 red out of 4 that is 3/4 x 2/3 = 6/12 = 1/2. No smaller total works, so 4 (with 3 red) is the minimum.
